subject: Re: Observability credits & retention — restructure proposal
messages:
From: Adam Lytton <adam.lytton@fortehealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fortehealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observability credits & retention — looking to restructure

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the advanced dashboards look promising. We ran our usage projections with the team and the current observability add-on SKU skews expensive once our retention window is extended beyond 90 days.

Two asks from procurement:
- Can you propose a commit/credit structure that smooths cost for our 12‑month forecast? We expect a surge in tracing during onboarding but steady longtail for retention.
- Is there a path to reduce or waive the one‑time integration fee if we commit to a minimum spend?

Attaching a small sample of last quarter's retention/trace usage for reference (Forte-Usage-Sample.csv).

Can we get a short proposal by EOD Monday? We need numbers for our budget review.

Best,
Adam Lytton
Head of Platform Engineering
Forte Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Adam Lytton <adam.lytton@fortehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability credits & retention — looking to restructure

Hi Adam — thanks for the note and the sample usage. Attaching a short pricing workbook that lays out two alternative concession paths (RI-OBS-Pricing-Rev2.xlsx). High level:

Option A — Commit Credits (volume-first):
- 12‑month committed credits that convert to retention/storage and trace consumption.
- Accelerated discounts kicked in at 1.5x projected average monthly usage.
- Waived integration fee above $120k annual commit.

Option B — Hybrid smoothing (burst buffer + metered):
- Smaller commit covering longtail retention (90% of baseline).
- Pay‑as‑you‑go credits for burst tracing; discounted bucket pricing for retained traces beyond 90 days.
- One‑time integration fee reduced to 50% with 6‑month commit.

A few notes and open questions for you:
- How important is an exact mapping of credits to invoices vs. a single blended credit line? We can produce either.
- Do you need itemized per‑environment billing (prod/staging) for chargeback?

Proposed next step: 30‑minute call to pick a path and I’ll convert the chosen option into an amendment (SOW-credits-amendment-draft.pdf) with sample invoice lines. Are you available 11/30 or 12/1?

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555‑0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Adam Lytton <adam.lytton@fortehealth.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability credits & retention — looking to restructure

Adam — looping in a couple of pricing levers we can take on the product side to lower unit economics if you lean into a commit:

- Prefix + KV cache crediting: for onboarding bursts we can give a short‑term cache credit that materially reduces per‑token tracing cost for the first 90 days.
- Tracing sample windows: if you can tolerate 95% fidelity instead of 100% for longtail traces, we can apply a sampling tier that lowers storage by ~30%.
- Volume‑based seat discount: bundling advanced dashboards and tracing under a single commitment unlocks a seat/consolidation discount that compounds with credits.

I added estimates into Chloe's workbook (see RI-OBS-Pricing-Rev2.xlsx tab "Levers"), and flagged the clause in the amendment template where we can waive the integration fee subject to legal review. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/78342 for your reference.

If it helps, we can produce a sample invoice (line items) and a simple amortization schedule that shows monthly cashflow for commitments vs. PAYG. Chloe — I can draft that after you pick A or B.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Adam Lytton <adam.lytton@fortehealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fortehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T14:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability credits & retention — looking to restructure

Thanks Chloe and Ben — appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed both options with finance and procurement.

We prefer Option B (Hybrid smoothing) because it gives us flexibility during onboarding spikes while capping longtail retention spend. A couple of fast asks before legal signs an amendment:
- Can you provide a sample invoice for Option B with monthly amortization and the reduced integration fee column split? (We want to show the CFO the cashflow impact.)
- Please confirm how long you keep raw logs vs. indexed tracing metadata in the retention model — SOC/Privacy will need this for our data map.
- Confirm that credits applied to burst tracing will be visible on the HubSpot invoice line (we need itemization).

If you can drop the sample invoice and the short retention note into the Drive doc and send over a redlineable SOW, Procurement will aim to return a countersign within 5 business days.

Best,
Adam
Head of Platform Engineering
Forte Health
